content.note: Verified October 10, 2026 against statutes, session laws and revenue-agency schedules.

content: Included: changes in signed law that take effect on a stated date for tax years 2027 and later without any further determination: rate and bracket changes, phase-downs written as a series of years, statutory deductions and exclusions, sunsets of temporary rates, and a new tax.

Excluded: reductions that wait on a revenue trigger or another future determination. They are listed under "Not modeled" with the statute and the trigger. A trigger is modeled only once it is certified for a specific year.
For tax year Y, every change of the state with `year <= Y` applies in ascending order and replaces only the fields it sets.

Indexing: the state layer grows built-in amounts with the projection's calendar inflation factor (1.0 in 2026). Amounts a change keeps from 2026 (`dollar_year` 2026) keep growing from 2026. Amounts a statute sets in dollars for a later year (`dollar_year` = that year) equal the statutory amount in that year and grow afterwards. Nebraska and Montana index by statute; Mississippi, New York, Hawaii, Virginia and Washington's deduction before 2029 are not indexed by statute, and the engine keeps its existing convention of growing them.

User scheduled `state_brackets` and custom state brackets replace built-in law in the years they cover; with custom brackets the 2026 entry (no enacted changes) supplies the remaining built-in figures.

Opt-in statutory deduction rules (`state_deduction_rules_2026.json`) cover AL, MO, OR, CT and WI. None of those states has an enacted dated change for 2027 and later, so the rules stay 2026-based without conflict.
Part-year residency selects the year's state; that state's tables for the year include its enacted changes.

The act is void if a court of final jurisdiction invalidates the tax; litigation status is not tracked here.

content.condition: Rate falls 0.5 point per year (3.49% for 2027, 2.99% for 2028, floor 2.49%) only when General Fund revenue for the prior fiscal year exceeds the trigger ($33.042B for FY 2025-26 → tax year 2027), as reported in the State Controller's final accounting. The May 2026 consensus forecast projects the 2027 and 2028 triggers will be met; no certified determination was found. https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-153.7.html

From 2027: rate −0.125 point a year to 3.99%; standard deduction +$375 single / +$750 joint a year to $18,000 / $36,000; dependent exemption +$125 to $6,000. Each step is delayed a year whenever the Office of Planning and Budget finds by December 1 that the revenue-estimate, collections or reserve tests fail.
From 2031, further 0.2-0.3 point cuts when the reserve fund is full and adjusted revenue exceeds appropriations by set margins.

Each further cut needs the statutory fiscal tests and an act of the General Assembly; the 2026 session enacted none (2026 HB 13, graduated rates, died in committee).
0.1-point cuts when net general revenue beats the prior three years by $200M and the inflation test.
Annual rate reduction only when general fund growth exceeds inflation; determined each year.
